findings.reason: the very next dispatch the plan recommends would write `recovery_watch.py` before the node §14 says it must follow, so either §14 lands out of its declared order or the followup's order line must name §14 after §9's wiring node.
findings.text: the open followup `f-alwh-002` is titled "Build §14 next" and recommends `/reckon-build a-live-worker-is-never-drawn-halted §14`, but §14 (:329) states "It runs after §4, before §5 and §7, and after §9's wiring node, which also writes `recovery_watch.py`", and §9's wiring node is not built (§9 is `implementable`; comment `c-s9-node1` says only the first node landed); the followup's own shared-file order names §9's wiring node as a writer of `recovery_watch.py` and `runs.py` with "§13 runs after it" and omits §14, the second writer of `recovery_watch.py`

findings.reason: as written the instruction cannot be implemented; the node must either add an argument-taking normaliser to `fleet_supervisor` or be told to keep the `split(".")[0]` form `_hosts_match` already uses, and the plan currently says neither.
findings.text: §9's added done-when directs that "`_hosts_match` uses `fleet_supervisor._short_hostname`", but `fleet_supervisor._short_hostname` (fleet_supervisor.py:269-271) takes no argument and returns only the current host's short name, while `_hosts_match(host, node)` must normalise two arbitrary names — the foreign run's `launcher_host` and the fleet record's node — and `producer_start_decision` accepts an injected `host`

findings.reason: without the word's mapping the central new row of the section has no defined rendering, and mapping it into `delivered` would make it a same-word row the noise rules are meant to suppress, which changes the section's own expected output.
findings.text: §14 requires the review's start to be "drawn on the reviewed run as `delivered → in review`" and the done-when asserts "its `in review` row naming the review run", but `in review` is not a member of any `PANE_STATES` set (ticker.py:278-330) and `_display_state` returns "" for an unknown word, so `_pane_word` gives the row no pane word; the plan never says whether `in review` becomes its own pane state or maps into the existing `delivered` word, and that choice decides whether the row survives the same-word rule and the departure hold
